official.deadline_note: December 1 is the deadline for both counselor and nominee materials in all nominating regions; the Foundation communicates deadlines to nominators and nominees by email, and the scholarship calendar runs separately from UVA admissions.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 selection process (nomination portal opened August 2026; final Selection interviews February 2027, for students entering UVA in fall 2027)
official.status_note: The nomination portal opened in August 2026 for eligible schools and counselor/nominee materials are due December 1, 2026; the Foundation reports 2025-26 cycle highlights of 7,697 invited secondary schools across 85 regions, 3,289 nominated students, and $14,500,000 awarded in undergraduate support.
official.tuition_coverage_note: FAQ: 'The scholarship includes tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses based on full-time enrollment for eight semesters at the University of Virginia.' The scholarships page adds that the award 'is intended to cover the entire cost of attendance for four years at the University of Virginia, plus coverage of supplemental enrichment experiences.'
benefits: The award is intended to cover the entire cost of attendance for four years at the University of Virginia, plus coverage of supplemental enrichment experiences
Includes tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses based on full-time enrollment for eight semesters
Non-Virginians receive over $83,000 per year or upwards of $405,000 total; Virginians receive over $42,000 per year or upwards of $230,000 total

Enrichment opportunities: international travel, career development and networking, Institute for Leadership and Citizenship, alumni connections, Exploratory Fund, research collaboration with Jefferson Fellows, and Speaker Series
eligibility: No one may apply; eligible schools are asked to nominate a student in the senior class who best exemplifies excellence in leadership, scholarship, and citizenship
The nominee must gain admission to the University of Virginia through the Office of Undergraduate Admission
Jefferson and Walentas Scholars do not have to be U.S. citizens; the Foundation states it has Scholars from all over the globe
Prior interest in UVA and financial need are not factors in selecting a nominee, and no financial information is used in the selection process
Accepting a school's nomination only signals willingness to proceed; nominees are under no obligation to accept an offered scholarship
requirements: Counselor submits: basic nominee information, scholastic information about the school, one letter of recommendation, transcript, and school profile
Nominee submits: contact information, activities, awards, and two essays - a personal statement and a leadership essay
SAT, ACT, AP, and IB scores are not considered for the 2026-2027 selection process; UVA remains test optional
Applicant must separately apply to and gain admission to the University of Virginia; the Foundation has no access to the Common Application
documents: Two nominee essays: personal statement and leadership essay
Record of extracurricular activities and awards
University of Virginia admission application, submitted separately from the nomination portal
selection_criteria: Excellence or the potential for excellence as leaders, scholars, and engaged citizens
Three main components: Nomination, Regional Review, and Final Selection
Regional Selection Committees of alumni and friends of the University review transcripts, extracurricular activities, essays, and recommendations before determining who is interviewed
Finalists participate in a final virtual interview in late February (2027)
Admissions Review: the Office of Undergraduate Admission conducts an additional review of Early applicants and recommends nominees, who are notified in February
coverage: Entire cost of attendance for four years at UVA: tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses across eight semesters of full-time enrollment
Non-Virginians: over $83,000 per year, upwards of $405,000 total
Virginians: over $42,000 per year, upwards of $230,000 total
Supplemental enrichment experiences, including international travel and the Institute for Leadership and Citizenship
application_method: Nomination only through eligible high schools; there is no individual application. Counselors log in to the Foundation's nomination portal (https://login.jeffersonscholars.org)
Nominations are completed by both school officials and students and include a scholastic report, extracurricular activities, and two essays
Students from schools that have never nominated can contact selection@jeffersonscholars.org to establish eligibility
official.application_route: Nomination-only: a counselor at an eligible school nominates one senior via the Foundation portal by December 1, the student completes the nominee portion with two essays, and the student separately applies to and must be admitted by UVA.
official.citizenship_residency: No U.S. citizenship requirement; award value differs by residency (Virginians over $42,000 per year; non-Virginians over $83,000 per year)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - no U.S. citizenship is required; schools across the Foundation's nominating regions (85 regions invited in 2025-26) may nominate, and Walentas (first-generation) nominations come only from U.S. schools while non-U.S. schools may nominate for the Jefferson Scholarship
official.duration: Four years of undergraduate study at the University of Virginia (eight semesters of full-time enrollment)
official.description: The Jefferson Scholars Foundation attracts outstanding undergraduate students to the University of Virginia through the Jefferson Scholars Program and the parallel Walentas Scholars Program for first-generation students. The award is intended to cover the entire cost of attendance for four years at the University of Virginia, plus coverage of supplemental enrichment experiences, and is granted only to students nominated by eligible schools who gain admission to UVA.
official.region: North America (University of Virginia, Charlottesville); nominating regions worldwide
official.program_type: Nominative merit scholarship for University of Virginia undergraduates

applicant_utility.summary: There is no direct application - only a counselor at an eligible school can put you forward, so the first move is confirming your school sits in one of the nominating regions and raising it with your counselor during the autumn window. Counselor and nominee portions are both due December 1, 2026 in every region, and the Foundation runs its own calendar entirely separately from UVA admissions, so being admitted to UVA does not enter you into this competition. If you win, the package covers tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses for eight semesters, and no financial information is used at any point in selection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Seniors at invited schools, including international partner schools, with a sustained record of leadership and community engagement who want complete funding at UVA.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your school's eligibility in the region search on the selection page (over 65 Jefferson nominating regions) and alert your counselor early in the autumn term
Draft the two nominee essays - a personal statement and a leadership essay - well before December 1; they are the core content committees read
Confirm your counselor can supply your transcript, the school profile, and one recommendation without last-minute scrambling
File the separate UVA admission application on your own timeline; the Foundation cannot see your Common Application
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the UVA admission application doubles as the scholarship application - the two processes are completely separate
Counselor-side materials arriving after December 1; the date is identical in all regions and is communicated to nominators by email
Essays that list titles and hours instead of demonstrating community impact - committees screen for engaged citizenship, not paperwork
Schools that have never nominated before assuming they are locked out; the Foundation invites new schools to contact selection@jeffersonscholars.org
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package covers tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses for eight semesters, so personal spending and any travel outside approved enrichment activities are the main out-of-pocket items.
document_audit: The counselor, not the student, uploads the scholastic report, transcript, school profile, and letter of recommendation
Two distinct essays are nominee-submitted: a personal statement and a separate leadership essay
SAT, ACT, AP, and IB scores are not considered for the 2026-2027 process, so missing test scores will not stall an application
Accepting a nomination carries no obligation to accept the scholarship if it is later offered
alerts: December 1, 2026 is a hard deadline in all regions; regional review and interviews then run mid-December through January
Final Selection interviews in late February 2027 are virtual without exception, so practise interviewing on camera
Recipients must decide whether to accept the offer by mid-April
Students outside the United States cannot be nominated for the sibling Walentas first-generation scholarship - only for the Jefferson Scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Counselor and student each complete their own portal sections by December 1; regional alumni committees review files and interview from mid-December to January; finalists are interviewed virtually in late February and notified of the outcome before decisions are required in mid-April.

official.citizenship_residency: Open to international students on F-1 or other valid non-immigrant visas (H-4, L-2, E-2, TD); students who qualify for Minnesota resident tuition rates via approved residency or reciprocity in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Dakota, or Manitoba are not eligible

official.duration: Up to four years for freshmen; up to three years for transfer students
official.description: Global Excellence Scholarships are competitive, merit-based scholarships awarded to international freshmen and transfer students at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities. They provide up to four years of an undergraduate non-resident tuition waiver that can be applied only toward tuition costs; the University states it does not offer a full tuition waiver or scholarship and assumes international students will take full responsibility for financing their education.
official.program_type: Merit-based university scholarship for international undergraduates
official.english_requirement: Minimum for admission: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with a 6.5 writing subscore (Duolingo 120, PTE Academic 59, and C1 Advanced 180 are also accepted; scores effective starting the Spring 2027 application period). The test may be waived for applicants from exempt English-speaking countries, ACT/SAT thresholds, qualifying accelerated high school English curricula, or U.S. transfer coursework.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship essay to write: every admitted international freshman or transfer on an F-1 (or H-4, L-2, E-2, TD) whose admission file is complete by a deadline and who has filed the Certification of Finances form is reviewed automatically. Aim for the November 1 Early Action I deadline, because the award is tuition-only - housing, food, insurance, travel, and personal expenses stay on your budget, and the University states plainly that it offers no full scholarship. Renewal depends on keeping a valid visa status and at least 12 credits per semester, so treat continuous full-time enrollment as part of the deal.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international freshmen and transfers who can cover living costs themselves and want a partial tuition waiver at a major U.S. research university.
application_readiness_checklist: File the Common App by November 1 (Early Action I) - later rounds erode scholarship consideration
Submit the Certification of Finances form with the admission application; an incomplete file is not reviewed
Complete the Self-Reported Transcript and Academic Record (STARS) for freshmen
Test the English proficiency exemption routes before paying for IELTS - exempt-country, ACT/SAT, high-school curriculum, and U.S. transfer-credit routes can waive the test
Transfers: apply by the February 1 fall priority deadline, since a spring start is funds-available only
common_rejection_risks: Missing the deadline - especially transfers, where late applications are reviewed on a space-available basis
Qualifying for Minnesota resident or reciprocity tuition rates in MN, WI, ND, or Manitoba, which disqualifies you outright
Letting visa status lapse, since renewal requires maintaining valid non-immigrant status
Budgeting as if the award covers living costs; it can be applied only toward tuition and not to study abroad terms
Dropping below 12 credits per semester or falling into academic probation, which breaks the renewal criteria
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing, meals, health insurance, books, travel to and from the U.S., and personal expenses; the waiver applies only to tuition and cannot be used for study abroad.
document_audit: The Certification of Finances form is the most commonly forgotten item - without it you are not considered at all
TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted; report the highest overall and subscores from a single test date
An AZ hold means one supportive English course in the first semester, not loss of admission - clear it by passing the course or the MELP Minnesota Battery Test on arrival
Changing major or college does not affect the award, so enrollment flexibility is preserved
alerts: Freshmen recipients are notified by the end of March and transfer awards in May-June; the amount is fixed at admission and cannot be increased mid-degree
Renewal requires full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits per semester (30-credit annual requirement) and satisfactory academic progress
A leave of absence breaks the consecutive-enrollment requirement; appeal to admissions@umn.edu, but continuation is not guaranteed
Spring-entry transfers are considered only on a funds-available basis
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Common App by the applicable deadline plus the Certification of Finances form; the Office of Admissions reviews every admitted eligible international student automatically, and the award notice arrives by email with an Application Tracker login by the end of March.
